items.title: Ram, Jeep parent Stellantis reports profit and sales jump, but only reaffirms full-year guidance
items.summary: Ram, Jeep, and Fiat parent company Stellantis reported decent first-half results on Thursday morning, but only reaffirmed its prior guidance. Investors clearly want more from CEO Antonio Filosa's turnaround plan.

items.title: What F Holders Got Paid While The Stock Fell Behind
items.summary: The automaker sent a fortune back to its owners while the stock trailed the market, raising a sharp question about what those checks actually bought.

items.title: Trump Admits His New Tariffs Achieve the Same Goal as the Ones the Supreme Court Struck Down— Just 'A Harder Way'
items.summary: President Donald Trump said that his administration’s newly imposed U.S. tariffs are effectively the same as the tariffs the Supreme Court ruled illegal earlier this year. On Tuesday, in an interview with Fox News, Trump said, "It’s a shame that...

items.title: O'Reilly Q2 Earnings Beat on Strong Comparable and Pro Sales
items.summary: ORLY beats Q2 earnings and revenue estimates as strong comparable sales and pro customer growth help lift its 2026 outlook.

items.title: LAD Q2 Earnings Beat on Used Margins and Financing Growth
items.summary: Lithia Motors tops Q2 estimates as stronger used-vehicle margins, aftersales growth and record financing income offset mixed sales trends.

items.title: Tesla Eyes Its Worst July as Cathie Wood Buys the Dip. Who’s Right?
items.summary: Tesla is trading near a 52-week low after a brutal earnings week, and Cathie Wood just loaded up on shares while most investors are heading for the exits. The bull and bear cases have never been further apart.

items.title: General Motors is driving toward supply chain resiliency
items.summary: The automaker is upping its domestic production investments while securing memory supply to shield rising commodity and logistics costs.

items.title: Ford Motor Stock Can Keep Climbing Without Selling More Vehicles
items.summary: A high-margin subscription and parts business compounding behind the trucks is the strongest reason Ford stock's climb can continue.
